body:
packages/tickets/lib/manifest-segments.mjs's forestChainsIntact (and its per-chain helper chainIsIntact) is a duplicated, deliberately narrower mirror of @adlc/gate-manifest/lib/verify.mjs's verifyChain/verify -- it checks seq/prev hash-chain continuity and, when a key is given, per-chain signed-continuity, but explicitly skips (per its own doc comment) anchor placement (only the first entry of a segment may carry one), anchor resolution (does the anchor actually point at a real, matching line), empty-segment rejection, root-anchor prohibition, and cross-segment cycle detection. recordSegmentedTicketEvidence (evidence.mjs) and migrateSegmentedSet (ticket-sync/lib/reassign.mjs) both treat forestChainsIntact returning true as their sole precondition before mutating the ticket store, appending evidence, and deleting the transaction's recovery journal. A forest that forestChainsIntact accepts but gate-manifest's own verify() rejects (e.g. a segment with a dangling or duplicate anchor, an anchor pointing at the wrong chain, or a cycle) lets a ticket transaction finalize -- and its recovery journal disappear -- against evidence that the authoritative gate later refuses. Surfaced by a distinct-provider adversarial review (Codex) of PR #411 (T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3); confidence 0.98-0.99, HIGH severity, confirmed independently across two review rounds with slightly different framing each time. This mirrors an EXISTING, accepted tradeoff for the pre-segments root-only path (gate-manifest's own record.mjs likewise never runs a full verify() before every append, only a lighter continuity check), so it is not a strictly new class of risk -- but the segmented forest adds anchor/cycle invariants the root-only path never had to reason about, and the ticket-side duplicate has not caught up. Deliberately deferred rather than patched inline in slice 3: closing the gap correctly needs either importing gate-manifest's real verifyChain (which the package-cycle constraint documented at the top of manifest-segments.mjs currently forbids -- tickets has no dependencies and gate-manifest depends on tickets via core) or hand-porting anchor/cycle logic byte-for-byte and pinning it with a parity test, neither of which is a safe last-minute addition to an already-large trust-root-tier PR.

Acceptance criteria:
1. forestChainsIntact (or its replacement) rejects every forest shape gate-manifest verify() rejects: a segment whose first entry lacks the required anchor, a non-first entry that carries one, an anchor pointing at a line that does not exist or does not match, an empty segment file, a root entry carrying an anchor, and an anchor cycle. Verify: new tests, one per rejected shape, each proving forestChainsIntact now agrees with gate-manifest's own verify() on the identical fixture.
2. A round-trip parity test exists that runs the SAME set of forest fixtures through both forestChainsIntact and gate-manifest's verify(), asserting their valid/invalid verdicts always agree -- so a future drift between the two implementations fails a test instead of silently reopening this gap. Verify: node --test on the new parity test file.
3. Full suite green: npm test.
title: Bring forestChainsIntact into full parity with gate-manifest's authoritative verify() (T-MANIFEST-FOREST)
